facts.content: Patient reports feeling 'run-down' with cough and cold for 4–5 days.
Patient has a dry cough with minimal sputum in the morning.
Patient has rhinorrhea and sore throat, worsened by shouting.
Patient reports shortness of breath without chest pain.
Patient experiences intermittent fever/rigors at night.
Patient had 1-day diarrhea on day 1, now resolved.
Patient has diffuse muscle and joint pains (myalgias/arthralgias).
Patient's appetite is intact and they report increased fluid intake.
Patient has Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
Patient has hypertension.
Patient is obese.
Patient takes Metformin.
Patient takes Lisinopril.
Patient occasionally takes Aspirin (ASA).
Patient has no known allergies.
Patient lives with wife and is a factory worker.
Patient consumes approximately 9 pints of beer per week and is cutting down cigarettes, using vape.
facts.source_text: etOH ~9 pints beer/wk. Cutting down cigarettes; uses vape.

facts.content: The impression is viral upper respiratory tract infection or early influenza vs mild lower respiratory tract infection.

facts.content: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus is stable on Metformin.
Hypertension is stable on Lisinopril.
Patient is obese.
Tobacco and alcohol use.
Advised rest, hydration, and regular Paracetamol.
Delayed prescription of Amoxicillin 1 tab PO TID to start if no improvement in 24–48 hours or worsening shortness of breath.

facts.content: Patient to return if symptoms persist more than one week or if red flags such as increased shortness of breath, chest pain, or high fever appear.

facts.content: Continue Metformin and Lisinopril; maintain follow-up with PCP for diabetes and blood pressure; advise weight management.
